To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can: (1) automatically extract a large number of N-ary relations between Wikipedia articles; (2) learn a class hierarchy from Wikipedia categories, and (3) recommend new articles to the target KB, based on the network of the existing ones.

1) crowdsourced Frame Semantics annotation is a viable and effective solution for N-ary Relation extraction, 2) a taxonomy learning approach can be successfully applied to the Wikipedia category graph to produce an intuitive class hierarchy, 3) a recommender engine can be implemented to leverage a KB network to produce suggestions for real-world users, and 4) a combination of these three approaches can yield an effective and efficient way to populate a KB.

(1) the proposed crowdsourcing methodology is able to achieve a high inter-annotator agreement, (2) the N-ary Relation extraction system outperforms stateof-the-art systems on the target KB by 20%, (3) the taxonomy learning system outperforms the current state-ofthe- art on the task of classifying the target KB entities into a taxonomy, and (4) the recommender system achieves a high accuracy on the task of recommending atypical suggestions
